data.title: Heuremen Launches QuantumIdleAudit.com: Check the Hardware Before You Trust the Answer
data.description:
Heuremen Launches QuantumIdleAudit.com: Check the Hardware Before You Trust the Answer

Heuremen LLC launches quantumidleaudit.com, a calibration service for teams running on commercial cloud quantum processors.

Quantum processors change from day to day. Their published error figures miss some of that change. A research team plans a run on those figures, pays for the shots and never learns what the hardware actually did.

Quantum Idle Audit closes that gap. One short measurement job runs before the client's run. It reads what the processor actually delivers that day: gate error, readout error and the disturbance a readout causes on nearby qubits. Then the service calibrates the client's own circuit to those numbers. The client keeps its code, its algorithm and its processor.

Heuremen tested the service in two rounds on three commercial cloud quantum processors. Against the default run in each industry, the calibrated run:

  • cut option-pricing error 2.5 to 15 times
  • cut molecular energy error 3.6 to 3.9 times, and more than 5 times on the best processor
  • shrank the gap to the noiseless logistics answer 1.4 to 2 times
  • brought physics simulations 1.3 to 3.8 times closer to the exact answer
  • cut logical error in error correction by up to 1.7 times

More shots don't fix the default option price. Pooling every shot from 32 repeat runs still left it 6 to 23 percent off. The calibrated price landed within 4.4 percent.

The measurement also caught what the published figures missed. One qubit in a demonstration layout misread about one reading in 20, in both rounds. Its published figure said one in 1,000.

Machine-learning teams face a budget surprise too. At 40 qubits, a quantum kernel classifier needs 3.6 to 12 times the shots a plan from published gate errors budgets for. A 23-second check tells the team the real bill before it spends.

Heuremen means "we found it." We found these effects on real hardware, not in a simulator. Every number in this release links to its job records and checks at quantumidleaudit.com, so anyone can check our work.

About Heuremen LLC

Heuremen LLC builds independent measurement tools for research and computing. Quantum Idle Audit is its quantum calibration service.

data.title: Inside VinFast’s Net-Zero Climate Commitment
data.description:
Inside VinFast’s Net-Zero Climate Commitment

An electric bus partnership in the U.S. and expanded sales and service options for drivers show how VinFast is putting its electric mobility strategy into practice. The company’s published climate roadmap outlines how it plans to reduce emissions as the business grows.

While some automakers have scaled back their North American EV ambitions, VinFast continues to view electric vehicles as essential to addressing climate change. In the U.S. and Canada, the company is focused on making EVs easier to purchase, charge and service while helping customers understand operating costs. Its broader strategy centers on building a network of vehicles, charging infrastructure and services that can support more drivers and fleets over time.

One of the latest steps came on October 6, 2026, when VinFast announced an initial agreement with NexMove at the APTA TRANSform & EXPO in Chicago to bring its electric buses to U.S. customers. NexMove, a joint venture between Transportation Management Services and Zeem Solutions, plans to bundle buses, charging, maintenance and operations in a single agreement. It intends to offer a 97% uptime service-level commitment, with certified bus deliveries expected to begin in the first quarter of 2028. The announcement followed VinFast’s September 2026 franchise agreements for three U.S. dealerships in California and Pennsylvania.

Making electric mobility practical for fleets and drivers

For a transit agency, introducing electric buses requires decisions about depot charging, maintenance schedules and daily vehicle availability. NexMove’s proposed service brings these elements together into one agreement. Ahead of certified deliveries, NexMove plans to place demonstration buses at Zeem’s charging depots, where transit agencies and fleet operators can evaluate the vehicles firsthand. The demonstration units are intended for evaluation, with certified vehicles to follow on the planned delivery schedule.

VinFast’s buses combine camera- and radar-based driver assistance, fast charging capabilities, lithium iron phosphate batteries and corrosion protection. The company reported that approximately 2,000 of its electric buses were operating in Vietnam at the time of the announcement. VinFast’s experience in the market spans manufacturing, operations and maintenance, giving it firsthand knowledge of the demands fleet operators face when vehicles are in daily service.

“Bringing VinFast electric buses to the United States marks an important next step in our long-term commitment to this market,” said Brian Finnerty, CEO of VinFast North America.

For households, the questions are more personal: How much will it cost to charge a vehicle each month? Where can it be serviced? What options are available at a price the buyer can afford? The franchise agreements in Redondo Beach and Tustin, California, and Philadelphia, Pennsylvania, expand access to sales and after-sales service. The company’s U.S. certified pre-owned program gives buyers another option when weighing the upfront cost of an EV.

In Canada, VinFast offers a 10-year or 200,000-kilometre limited new-vehicle warranty on the VF 8, whichever comes first. Its online energy-cost calculator allows shoppers to compare estimated EV charging costs with the fueling costs of a gasoline vehicle over their expected mileage and ownership period. The comparison gives buyers a clearer picture of how an EV could fit their driving habits and household budget.

Annual EV charging costs can be 50% or more below gasoline fueling costs, depending on electricity rates, whether drivers charge at home or use public stations, driving habits, and vehicle efficiency. Coltura’s Q3 2024 analysis estimated that U.S. EV drivers saved an average of 7.4 cents per mile on fuel. At 1,200 miles a month, that works out to about $90 a month, or nearly $1,100 a year if the same per-mile savings hold.

Why a long-term climate commitment matters as markets change

VinFast announced its transition to all-electric vehicle production at CES in Las Vegas in 2022. Just over two years later, it became Vietnam’s best-selling vehicle brand in 2024, according to Vingroup’s annual report. Its expansion into North America brings a different set of considerations, including where to build out sales and service operations, how to support charging infrastructure and how to help commercial customers integrate electric vehicles into their existing operations.

Incentives, regulations and customer demand can change while a factory upgrade or charging project is still in development. VinFast’s 2040 net-zero goal provides a long-term framework for investments that take years to plan and implement. For example, the timing of an equipment replacement affects when a plant can shift more of its operations to electricity. The source of that electricity then affects the emissions associated with running the equipment. Decisions about materials and suppliers have a similar bearing on emissions across the value chain.

VinFast’s emissions inventory illustrates why those decisions matter as production grows. The company calculated that its emissions exceeded 1.12 million metric tons of carbon dioxide equivalent (CO₂e) in its 2022 base year. In a separate scenario, VinFast estimated that emissions could exceed 20 million metric tons of CO₂e if its existing production operations in Vietnam reached their maximum registered capacity, excluding future factories. The estimate illustrates the importance of factoring energy efficiency, electricity sourcing and supplier emissions into plans for higher production.

How the 3E Mission puts the 2040 pledge into practice

VinFast signed The Climate Pledge on August 17, 2022, and announced its participation in September 2022. It was the first Vietnamese enterprise to sign the pledge, an initiative co-founded by Amazon and Global Optimism. The company’s stated goal is to reach net-zero emissions by 2040 across Scopes 1, 2 and 3, covering direct emissions from its operations, indirect emissions from purchased energy, and emissions across its wider value chain. Signatories commit to measuring and reporting greenhouse gas emissions regularly, reducing emissions and neutralizing the remainder.

In January 2025, VinFast’s chairwoman approved the company’s net-zero strategy through 2030, with a view to 2040. The strategy centers on the 3E Mission, which sets out how VinFast plans to change the equipment it uses, reduce the energy it needs and source cleaner power.

  • Electrification. VinFast plans to electrify equipment at company-owned production and business sites by 2030. The roadmap also includes expanding access to charging and developing battery energy storage.
  • Energy Saving. VinFast plans to introduce smart energy monitoring at manufacturing facilities by 2028. Monitoring production lines and major electricity-consuming equipment gives factory teams more detailed information on where energy is used and where operations can be made more efficient.
  • Energy Greening. VinFast aims to use 100% renewable electricity at all its plants by 2040. Its roadmap includes rooftop solar, battery storage to support renewable power use, and work with suppliers on lower-emission materials.

VinFast’s manufacturing complex in Hai Phong offers a practical example of what these priorities translate to on the factory floor. The company reported that upgrades to lighting and compressed-air systems, changes to how production robots operate, and other efficiency measures saved approximately 2.7 million kilowatt-hours of electricity in 2024, equivalent to an estimated 1,782 metric tons of CO₂e.

The company also said it initiated a 30-megawatt-peak rooftop solar project at the site. While the efficiency measures address how much electricity the plant needs, the solar project addresses the source of the electricity.

Against its 2022 baseline, VinFast aims to reduce Scope 1 and 2 emissions by 42% and Scope 3 emissions by 29% by 2030. By 2040, the strategy calls for cutting total emissions by at least 85% and neutralizing residual emissions of up to 15% through carbon offsetting mechanisms, which could include carbon credits. As VinFast serves more drivers and fleets, its reported emissions will show how far the company has progressed toward those targets across its operations, purchased energy and value chain.

data.title: Folding Bikes Were Never Built for Everyone? DAHON is Fixing That
data.description:
Folding Bikes Were Never Built for Everyone? DAHON is Fixing That

Folding Bikes Were Never Built for Everyone? DAHON is Fixing That

PR Newswire

SACRAMENTO, Calif., Nov. 26, 2026

SACRAMENTO, Calif., Nov. 26, 2026 /PRNewswire/ -- For over forty years, DAHON has offered freedom that fits more riders. Behind that mission is Founder and CEO Dr. David Hon, whose entrepreneurial journey began in laser research.

DAHON's ultra-light folding e-bike K-Feather made a splash when it was launched. Now the company's new Heavy Duty Folding Bike Series – Mariner XL and Mariner HD – are probably the first folding bikes built specifically for heavier riders, rated to offer 150 kg (330 lb) payload, roughly 40% higher than typical folding bikes.

The Road Not Taken – Physicist Turned Entrepreneur

A physicist at Hughes Research Laboratories, Dr. Hon was inspired by the 1970s oil crisis to pursue greener urban transport. "Initially, I wanted to license my patents, but no factory was willing to produce them. So, I raised funds on my own, built a factory to manufacture and market them," said Dr. Hon.

The first DAHON folding bicycle appeared in 1982, pioneering modern folding bicycle design and earning Dr. Hon recognition as the "Father of the Modern Folding Bicycle."

Dr. Hon had taken the road less travelled by. More than four decades on, and that has made all the difference.

Frame Flex Is Costing Riders Watts – DAHON Fixes That

Dr. Hon's scientific approach lives on in DAHON-V Tech, combining physics, computerized finite element analysis and strain gauges to evaluate bicycle stiffness.

DAHON's DELTECH cable and Super Down Tube can increase frame stiffness by 33% and riding speed by 5–15%, according to DAHON's internal testing. Results vary with test conditions and bicycle configuration.

Folding Bikes for All Riders, Aspirations Unchanged

From the approximately 12 kg K-Feather electric-assist folder to the Heavy Duty Series, DAHON is widening access to cycling. Its independent sub-brand BICECO targets the mass market.

Looking ahead, DAHON plans to advance DAHON-V Tech, expand its tri-fold carbon frame series and electric-assist ranges, and pursue targeted acquisitions in new materials and core technologies.

From solving the portability problem in 1982 to widening its international footprint today, the ambition has not changed: make cycling a practical, everyday choice.

About DAHON

Founded in California in 1982 by Dr. David T. Hon, DAHON is a global folding bicycle brand and pioneer of modern folding bikes. DAHON TECH is listed on HKEX (2543).

data.description:
ViaBTC to Showcase a Decade of Mining Expertise and One-Stop Asset Management at Blockchain Life 2026

ViaBTC to Showcase a Decade of Mining Expertise and One-Stop Asset Management at Blockchain Life 2026

PR Newswire

DUBAI, UAE, Nov. 26, 2026

DUBAI, UAE, Nov. 26, 2026 /PRNewswire/ -- ViaBTC, a leading global cryptocurrency mining pool, will participate in Blockchain Life 2026 on December 1–2 at Festival Arena in Dubai. Following its recognition as "Mining Pool of the Year" at Blockchain Life 2025, ViaBTC returns to discuss industry trends, pool infrastructure, and miner asset management with global partners.

Rising hashrate, higher electricity costs, and pressure on BTC revenues continue to challenge miners, even as institutional adoption, regulatory progress, and next-generation hardware reshape the sector. On December 2 at 12:25, Anton Tsarenok, ViaBTC's Business Development Director, will deliver a keynote titled "The Real State of Mining in 2026," examining mining economics and how pools support operational efficiency.

"Mining competition in 2026 is no longer just about hashrate. It also depends on operational efficiency and capital management," said Anton. "Pools must provide reliable infrastructure and practical tools to help miners manage earnings and working capital."

Since June 2016, ViaBTC's Bitcoin pool has maintained ten years of uninterrupted operation and one of the industry's lowest orphan rates. Globally distributed nodes support low-latency connections, while hashrate monitoring and alerts help identify issues promptly. Under ViaBTC's PPS+ model, PPS earnings from block subsidies are credited hourly, giving miners timely access to their earnings.

Beyond settlement, ViaBTC helps miners manage assets and working capital within their accounts. With Auto Conversion, available balances of supported coins convert into BTC or USDT hourly without manual transfers to an external exchange. For electricity or maintenance expenses, Collateral-Pledged Loans start from 50 USDT with flexible repayment and no fixed maturity date. Miners can redeem collateral once principal and interest are repaid.

At Booth A22, the ViaBTC team will meet mining operators, institutional clients, hardware manufacturers, and hosting providers. Visitors can explore subaccount management, read-only Watcher links, earnings allocation, tailored institutional services, and product demonstrations. Attendees are invited to visit the booth or arrange a meeting in advance via the ViaBTC website.

About ViaBTC

ViaBTC is a multi-cryptocurrency mining pool serving miners worldwide. Launched in 2016, it specializes in secure, stable, and efficient Proof-of-Work (PoW) mining services, supporting major PoW cryptocurrencies including BTC, LTC/DOGE, BCH, ZEC, and KAS. ViaBTC has served more than 2 million users across over 150 countries and regions. Its BTC, LTC/DOGE merged-mining, BCH, and ZEC pools rank among the world's leading mining pools.

data.title: Suspension of Mining and Processing Activities at the Tucumã Operation
data.description:
VANCOUVER, British Columbia, Nov. 26, 2026 (GLOBE NEWSWIRE) -- Ero Copper Corp. (TSX: ERO, NYSE: ERO) ("Ero" or the "Company") announces that all production activities, including mining and processing, at the Tucumã Operation have been temporarily suspended in compliance with a notice from the Pará State Environment and Sustainability Secretariat ("SEMAS").

Last week, the Tucumã Operation experienced significant rainfall events stemming from this year's very strong El Niño conditions, which overwhelmed the pumping capacity of a surface contact-water sump and resulted in two localized overflow events. The rainfall events were short in duration but included peaks above 70mm per hour. Significant rain events contributed to overall rainfall in the first 20 days of November that totaled approximately 275mm, as measured at the operation's weather station, approximately 170% above normal seasonal rainfall for the entire month of November. Upon identifying the overflow events, the Company promptly activated additional resources to increase water pumping and storage capacity along with relocating a stockpile to reduce the potential for additional contact water in the area affected by the overflows. The Company also notified SEMAS of the overflow events.

SEMAS conducted an independent technical assessment of the overflow events and notified the Company that it had identified anomalous pH readings in local water samples near the Tucumã Operation. SEMAS directed the Company to temporarily suspend mining operations; however, processing operations were permitted to continue while the Company engaged in active and constructive dialogue with SEMAS regarding continuity of mining and processing operations concurrent with remediation and planning efforts.

Despite stoppage of all production activities, constructive dialogue remains ongoing, and the Company expects to submit the final remediation plan requested by SEMAS for its review shortly. The Tucumã Operation is expected to resume activities following SEMAS's technical review and subsequent approval of the Company's proposed remediation plan. Fines associated with the overflow events totaled approximately US$2.9 million (BRL $16.8 million).

Weather conditions in October and this month have significantly impacted Pará State. Communities in and near the municipality of São Félix do Xingu, located approximately 50 km away from the Tucumã Operation, reported two separate fish mortality events prior to the aforementioned overflow events. The São Félix do Xingu municipal environment secretariat has issued a fine associated with these fish mortality events totaling approximately US$1.9 million (BRL $10.9 million). To date, Ero has not received documentation to support this fine, and no correlation between these events and the Tucumã Operation has been identified by Ero. The Company is working collaboratively with the technical agencies responsible for mining activities in the region.

Ero remains fully committed to remediation of the areas impacted by the overflow events, protecting the environment and contributing responsibly to the region.

ABOUT ERO

Ero is a Brazil-focused, growth-oriented mining company with a diversified portfolio of copper and gold assets. Headquartered in Vancouver, B.C., the Company operates two copper mines – the Caraíba Operations in Bahia State and the Tucumã Operation in Pará State – as well as the Xavantina Operations, a producing gold mine in Mato Grosso State. In addition to its operating assets, Ero is advancing the Furnas Copper-Gold Project, located in the mineral-rich Carajás Province in Pará State, through a definitive earn-in agreement with Vale Base Metals to acquire a 60% interest in the project.

Ero’s operating philosophy is grounded in a commitment to safety, operational excellence, and the responsible production of minerals essential for a better tomorrow. The Company’s shares are publicly traded on the Toronto Stock Exchange and the New York Stock Exchange under the symbol “ERO.” Additional information, including technical reports on the Company’s operations and projects, is available on the Company’s website (www.ero.com), SEDAR+ (www.sedarplus.ca), and on EDGAR (www.sec.gov).

FOR MORE INFORMATION, PLEASE CONTACT

Farooq Hamed, VP, Investor Relations
info@ero.com

data.title: China's Industrial Profit Surged Despite Headwinds
data.description:
China's industrial profit surged in October despite mounting domestic headwinds, as robust global demand for its tech products continued to turbocharge exports.

Profits at China's major industrial firms rose 20.1% from a year earlier in October, accelerating from the prior month's 14.4% growth, according to official data released Friday. During the first 10 months of the year, China's industrial profit jumped 16.0%.

Profit growth was powered by the electronics sector, according to the National Bureau of Statistics. Rising demand for artificial-intelligence computing power drove sustained profit gains across related industries, including memory chips and peripheral manufacturing, said Yu Weining, a senior official at the bureau.

During the January-to-October period, profits in the electronics sector doubled from a year earlier, contributing roughly 10 percentage points to overall profit growth among major industrial firms and serving as a key driver of their rapid expansion, said Yu.

Rapid growth in the new-energy and AI sectors also fueled strong demand and higher prices for base metals such as copper and aluminum from January to October, pushing profits up 60.2% from a year earlier in nonferrous metal mining and 71.7% across the broader nonferrous metals industry.

Friday's upbeat data contrasted with earlier data showing the world's second-largest economy lost momentum across multiple fronts in October, underscoring its uneven growth. Surging exports have obscured sluggish consumer demand, declining investment and a protracted property downturn.

Economists at ANZ said China's robust exports have failed to pass through to domestic demand. "Weak domestic demand has exacerbated both domestic and global imbalances, while persistent disinflation has kept onshore yields structurally low." they told clients in a note Friday.
